children: is investing an initial $250M in a global housing initiative that will unlock $5B in financing over the next 10 years to build rental housing developments and help address the shortage of affordable housing.

As part of its Airbnb Housing Accelerator initiative, the company is providing “last-dollar financing” in rental housing developments that are ready to build but “stuck on the one-yard line.” Research commissioned by Airbnb
estimates that 750K housing units across the country have cleared most regulatory hurdles but lack the final financing commitment needed to break ground.
The company said it will invest at returns "significantly" below standard market rates, prioritizing affordable and mixed-income housing projects that are stalled.
As part of the initiatives, Airbnb

will also support pro-housing policy reforms and will release a dataset designed to give interested parties, including policymakers, insight into the state of housing policies and outcomes across the country.
The first community with a $6.4M investment by Airbnb
will be in Austin, Texas, for the construction of 201 affordable housing units as part of the larger St. John redevelopment project.
In addition to investing capital in construction, Airbnb
will provide five $1M awards to innovators and entrepreneurs that have developed technologies and designs that make it easier, faster, and cheaper to build a home.

“The ability to afford housing is part of the foundation of Airbnb. The company was launched because we couldn’t afford our rent—and today, that reality exists for millions of Americans. The housing crisis wasn’t created overnight, and it won’t be solved overnight. But we can start moving in the right direction, and that is exactly what the Airbnb Housing Accelerator is designed to do,” said Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky.

title: Airbnb pledges $250M to boost affordable housing
